chunks.text: Welcome to the Slow English podcast.
Today we travel to Africa, but not to a big city, not to Nairobi.
Today we visit a small and quiet island town.
Lamu feels different from modern cities.
Lamu is in Kenya and East Africa.
It is on the coast of the Indian Ocean.
It is not easy to reach.
You take a small plane or a boat.
Part three, a town without cars.
Some streets are so small that two people walk carefully.
Lamu is very old and 700 years old.
It was part of the Swahili coast culture.
You can see this history in the buildings.
Lamu is important for Swahili culture.
Culture is not a show here.
Part six, the ocean and daily life.
The Indian ocean is very close.
You smell salt in the air.
Fishermen go out early in the morning.
In the evening, people sit near the water.
Part nine, the call to prayer.
Religion is part of daily life.
You hear the call to prayer.
The sound is soft and beautiful.
Even if you are not religious, you feel calm when you hear it.
Lamu has a special festival every year.
And there is something unique, a donkey race.
At night, Lamu becomes very quiet.
Part 12, the soul of Lamu and goodbye.
Lamu is not fast, but Lamu is real.
Life moves with nature, not against it.
In a world of speed, Lamu whispers, slow down.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English podcast.
See you in the next journey.
